paragraphs: Rav Pinchas son of Rav Chisda.

Hyman cites Kiddushin 32a for the wedding of Rava’s son. The corresponding passage is in [Kiddushin 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.32b.2). In Hyman’s account, Rav Pinchas and his brother Rav Mari were among the guests. If their father was the Rav Chisda usually meant by that name, Rava was their brother-in-law. Rava raised a cup to Rav Papa and to Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua, and they rose before him. He did the same for Rav Mari and Rav Pinchas, “son” of Rav Chisda, which Hyman would read as “sons.” They did not rise, and Rava took offense.

In [Ketubot 61a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.61a.15), Rav Pinchas and Rav Mari, sons of Rav Chisda, differ in when they serve the attendant his food. Elijah would speak with the one who served it early. In [Bava Kamma 117a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.117a.13), Hyman cites Rav Mari (מארי), son of Rav Pinchas, son of R. H. He reports the Dikdukei Soferim reading, “Rav Mari and R. P., sons of R. Ch.”[^1]

notes.text: The consulted Kiddushin has a singular “son of Rav Chisda” adjacent to Pinchas. The alternative in Ketubot has the plural. Davidson’s Bava Kamma gives Rav Mari son of Rav Pinchas son of Rav Chisda. Hyman’s initials and his reported apparatus variant remain distinct.
